Petitioners appeal a board of county commissioners 1 decision approving
2 modification of a destination resort final master plan.
3 RECORD OBJECTIONS
4 On June 5, 2023, the Board received the original record in this appeal. On
June 14, 2023, petitioner Gould (Gould) filed record objections. On June 16, 5
6 2023, petitioner The Confederated Tribes of the Warm Springs Reservation of
7 Oregon (CTWS) filed record objections. On June 20, 2023, we received from the
8 county a replacement record and table of contents.1 The certificate of service
9 attached to the replacement record states that it was served on the parties on June
10 15, 2023. Gould’s and CTWS’ (together, petitioners) record objections refer to
11 the replacement record and explain that it resolves, or partially resolves, many of
12 the record objections.2 On June 23, 2023, the county and intervenors-respondents
13 (together, respondents) filed joint responses to petitioners’ record objections. We
14 now resolve the objections.
1 The county explains: “This record replaces the original record filed on June
1, 2023. Video content provided in the original record remains the same,
however, a replacement April 17, 2023, video is concurrently submitted with this
amended record.” Face Page Replacement Record. We refer to the replacement
record as such, while the parties refer to it as the amended record.
2 The replacement record’s certificate of service and filing indicates that it was
served on Gould after Gould filed their record objections. We understand the
statements in Gould’s objections that the replacement record resolves their
objections to be anticipatory. See Gould Record Objection 3 (“Petitioner
conferred with the County and it appears some of the objections may be resolved,
or partially resolved in Respondent’s submittal of an amended record.”).
Page 4
1 A. Resolved Objections
Petitioners object that the original record page numbers are illegible. The 2
3 replacement record page numbers are legible. Petitioners agree that this issue is
resolved by the replacement record. These objections are resolved. 4
5 Petitioners object that the video recording of the April 17, 2023, county
6 board of commissioners meeting is incomplete. The replacement record contains
7 a video recording of the April 17, 2023, meeting.3 These objections are resolved.
8 B. Unresolved Objections
1. Table of Contents 9
10 Gould objects that the table of contents originally transmitted by the county
11 does not “correctly reflect the contents of the record.” Gould Record Objection
4. Gould asserts that the table of contents is deficient several ways and suggests 12
13 alternative titles for specific items. Gould indicates that the replacement record
14 table of contents resolves or partially resolves their objections.
15 OAR 661-010-0025(4)(a)(B) provides that the record must
16 “[b]egin with a table of contents, listing each item contained therein,
17 and the page of the record where the item begins (see Exhibit 2).
18 “(i) Where an item listed in the table of contents includes attached
19 exhibits, the exhibits shall be separately listed as an exhibit to
20 the item. Where the exhibit is also a document that is being
21 retained under OAR 661-010-0025(2), the exhibit shall also
3 CTWS states that the entire video is included in the replacement record and
withdraws its objection.

be listed at the end of the table of contents 1 as provided in
2 subsection (ii) below.
3 “(ii) Where large maps, media recordings, or other items or
4 documents are retained by the governing body under section
5 (2) of this rule, those retained items shall be separately listed
6 at the end of the table of contents[.]”
7 A table of contents meets the requirements of OAR 661-010-0025(4)(a)(B) where
8 “it is specific enough to enable the parties to locate individual documents in the
9 record with reasonable effort.” Rickreall Community Water Assoc. v. Polk
County, 52 Or LUBA 772, 776 (2006). We have reviewed the replacement record 10
11 table of contents and find that it is specific enough to be used with “reasonable
12 effort.” Id. Gould’s objections to the table of contents are denied to the extent
13 that they have not been resolved by the replacement record table of contents.

7 3. Meeting Minutes
8 CTWS objects that the minutes of the March 29, 2023, board of
9 commissioners meeting are incomplete. Our rules allow for “[a]n objection on
10 grounds that the minutes * * * are incomplete or inaccurate” where a party can
11 “demonstrate with particularity how the minutes * * * are defective and shall
12 explain with particularity why the defect is material.” OAR 661-010-0026(3). If
13 that burden is met, then
14 “the Board shall require the governing body to produce a transcript
15 of the relevant portion of the proceeding, if an audiotape recording
16 or other type of recording is available. Upon such demonstration
17 regarding contested transcripts, the Board shall require the
18 governing body to produce a more complete or amended transcript.”
19 Id.
20 CTWS quotes two portions of the minutes that indicate that the board
21 considered whether Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife (ODFW) and
22 CTWS approval of a modified fish and wildlife mitigation plan is “required
23 and/or a substantial consideration when determining if the ‘no net loss’ standard
24 is met[.]” Record 11. The minutes indicate that the board concluded that such
Page 7
approval is not required. Id. However, the minutes do not 1 indicate whether the
2 board determined whether ODFW and CTWS approval is a substantial
3 consideration. CTWS argues that those omissions in the minutes are material
4 because CTWS intends to argue that ODFW and CTWS approval is a substantial
consideration when determining whether the no net loss standard has been met. 5
6 CTWS does not argue that the board determined whether ODFW and
7 CTWS approval is a “substantial consideration.” Instead, CTWS observes that
8 the minutes do not indicate whether the board made those determinations. Thus,
9 we cannot conclude that the minutes are incomplete. That minutes are brief does
10 not mean that they are incomplete. See Port of Umatilla v. City of Umatilla, 70
11 Or LUBA 527, 530 (2014) (“Minutes of a proceeding are necessarily summary,
12 and are not expected to include specific arguments or details of oral statements.”).
13 To the extent that CTWS intends to rely on specific statements that are not
reflected in the minutes, CTWS may refer to the video recordings that are in the 14
15 record, and may attach a verbatim transcript to their petition for review. See OAR
16 661-010-0030(5) (“The petition for review may include appendices containing
17 verbatim transcripts of relevant portions of media recordings that are part of the
18 record.”). This objection is denied.

21 and intervenor-petitioner’s briefs shall be due 21 days after the date of this order.
